A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MAESTRO study, with 17 pages, eight figures, eight tables and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across seven benchmarks using two backbone models, including performance comparisons, training-time measurements and Conductor ablations (Tables 1–6).

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, timing measurements, ablations and learned reward-weight trajectories (Tables 1–6 and Figure 3).

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain the same terminal-hidden-state Conductor, five-reward scalarization, discrete training actions, continuous inference weights and asynchronous meta-updates.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Natural Reasoning, GeneralThoughts, WebInstruct, SS-GEN, EmoBench, ToMBench and OPUS-Books. No datasets, task requirements or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Base, SFT, CoT, NOVER, Eq, EM and Rand. Table 3 retains the Qwen3-32B LLM-as-a-Judge reward baseline; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same backbones, splits, preprocessing, DR-GRPO training settings, judge assignments and majority-vote evaluation protocol (Section 4.1 and Appendices C–F).

E4.justification: The input-layer, meta-loss and asynchronous-versus-joint training ablations in Tables 4–6 are unchanged, as is the reward-allocation analysis in Figure 3.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 retains three independent judge samplings with majority voting. Training-seed repetitions, confidence intervals and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figure 3 retain the same numerical results and trends. For example, Qwen3-8B scores remain 53.20% on NR and 92.52% on SS-GEN in Table 1.

T1.justification: Section 3's objectives and gradient formulation, Appendix A's mathematical argument, and the reward and optimization definitions in Appendices B, E and G are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about contextual reward orchestration, advantage-driven meta-learning, seven-benchmark performance and preservation of GRPO efficiency.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged. Section 7 retains limitations concerning reward quality, the five selected reward types and the need to verify scaling beyond the evaluated 8B models.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that MAESTRO's source code is publicly available and supplies a project repository address in the abstract. Implementation details, hardware and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes to citation author labels, titles, venues and identifiers, including the Qwen3, Llama 3 and DYNAOPT entries, are bibliographic revisions rather than new related work.

P1.justification: v2 adds the code-availability sentence and Section 8 Acknowledgements, shortens the contact-email list, corrects author-list punctuation and revises bibliographic metadata. The scientific narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Limited page and column reflow moves Table 5 from the left to the right column on page 8 and extends the conclusion onto page 9. Figures, tables and captions retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The added project-code address and funding acknowledgement modestly improve access documentation and transparency. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. Repository availability and completeness cannot be established from the supplied PDFs, so the supported improvement is limited to documentation.
